data.gender_notes: Purushottam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Purushottam is a name for the supreme personality of Godhead in Hinduism. It is a combination of 'Purusha' meaning 'person' and 'uttam' meaning 'supreme'. The name Purushottam carries the meaning “Supreme Personality of Godhead” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Purushottam usually hope their child will grow to embody supreme personality of godhead and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the ultimate divine reality and the source of all creation.
data.etymology: Purushottam belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Supreme Personality of Godhead.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Purushottam total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Purushottam holds a significant cultural importance in Hinduism as it is a revered name for Lord Vishnu, one of the primary deities in the Hindu pantheon. In many Hindu texts and scriptures, Purushottam is referred to as the embodiment of perfection, morality, and divinity.
data.spiritual_significance: For Hindus, the name Purushottam holds immense spiritual significance as it symbolizes the ultimate goal of life, which is to attain spiritual perfection and oneness with the divine. The name evokes feelings of reverence, devotion, and love towards the supreme being, inspiring one to lead a virtuous and righteous life, in the pursuit of Moksha or liberation from the cycle of birth and rebirth.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Purushottam symbolizes the supreme being or the ultimate purusha (embodiment of consciousness) within each individual. It signifies the highest realization of the self as pure consciousness and the attainment of a god-like state.

vedic_reference.note: One of the many names of Lord Vishnu in Hinduism.

historical_references.reference: Purushottam was a title given to Lord Vishnu in the Dwapara Yuga. He is depicted as the protector of the universe and the embodiment of morality and virtue. He is also known as Hari-Hara, a combination of Lord Vishnu and Lord Shiva.

Purushottam is also the name of the legendary king of Hastinapur in the Mahabharata epic. He was one of the five Pandava brothers and is known for his righteousness, bravery, and devotion to Lord Krishna.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Purushottam' is a revered title given to Lord Vishnu in Hinduism. It means 'supreme man' or 'perfect man'. In the modern context, this name is popularly used in devotional music, where various artists sing bhajans and compositions dedicated to Lord Purushottam. These songs are often streamed on digital music platforms like YouTube, Gaana, and Wynk Music. Additionally, the name is also explored in Hindu mythology and spirituality studies, both academically and within spiritual communities.

name_in_real_life.story: Amit Purushottam, a teacher in Hyderabad, India, shares that their name Purushottam meaning "Supreme Personality of Godhead" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
